etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English cotoun, from Anglo-Norman cotun, Old French coton, from (Genoese) Old Italian cotone, from Arabic قُطُن (quṭun).

definitions.definition: Gossypium, a genus of plant used as a source of cotton fiber.

quote.citation: 1976, Chuen-Yan David Lai, “Developments of Cotton Cultivation in Sinkiang”, in Pacific Viewpoint‎[1], volume 17, number 2, →DOI, archived from the original on 30 June 2020, page 162:
quote.text: K'a-shih has the most extensive cotton-growing area which amounted to 950 000 mou (6.3 million ares) in 1965.

definitions.definition: Any plant that encases its seed in a thin fiber that is harvested and used as a fabric or cloth.
Any fiber similar in appearance and use to Gossypium fiber.
(textiles) The textile made from the fiber harvested from a cotton plant, especially Gossypium.

quote.citation: 1963, Margery Allingham, chapter 2, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:

definitions.definition: (countable) An item of clothing made from cotton.

definitions.definition: Made of cotton.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To provide with cotton.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: 1560s, either from Welsh cydun, cytun (“agree, coincide”) (cyduno, cytuno), from cyd, cyt + un (“one”), literally “to be at one with”, or by metaphor with the textile, as cotton blended well with other textiles, notably wool in hat-making.

definitions.definition: (Should we move, merge or split(+) this sense?) To get on with someone or something; to have a good relationship with someone.
